title: Shopping cart design
idea: A shopping cart design keeps the cart as a list of product lines, and moves pricing, discounts and stock checks into separate classes that run at checkout.
points: `Cart` stores lines keyed by product id, so adding twice raises the quantity.
Money is held in whole cents, so adding prices never drifts like floats.
Discounts are strategies with one `discount(cart)` method, summed at checkout.
`Checkout` checks every line's stock first, then deducts, so orders never half-apply.

code.title: Cart, discount, checkout
code.caption: Prices are in cents. Add a `FlatOff` class that takes 200 cents off orders above 1000, and pass both rules.

walk.text: A `Map` keyed by sku merges repeated adds into one line.
The subtotal is computed from the lines each time, never stored and left stale.
A discount rule reads the cart and returns cents. It never edits the cart.
Validate every line first, then deduct stock, so a failure leaves nothing changed.
Sum all discount rules, then empty the cart once the order is placed.
Ana took the only mug, so Raj's checkout fails and stock stays correct.

pitfalls: Do not store prices as floats like `8.99`; use integer cents.
Re-check stock and price at checkout; the cart may be days old.
Do not put coupon `if` chains inside `Cart`; add a discount class instead.

quiz.why: Binary floats cannot hold 0.1 or 0.2 exactly, so their sum misses 0.3. Integers add exactly, which is why carts count cents.

takeaway: The cart holds lines; checkout validates, prices and deducts in one place.
